Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
The final table was full of noobs

Frédéric Pin (Escaped Mental Patient / Daemonic Possession) > Pierre Tran-Van (Hardestadt Alastor) > Tim Daudé (Khursid Legionnaire) > Arnaud Baigts (Ventrue Prince Grinder) > Vincent Ripoll (Stanislava)

At the end of the 3 rounds:

Pierre 2GW8
Vincent 2GW5
Tim 1GW4
Fred 1GW3.5
Arnaud 1GW3

Fred is first, which means he won't be able to bring out a EMP on his second turn. Luckily, I have a Information Highway, so I can bring out Stanislava on my second turn. Fred will try to bring down Hardestadt first, but Pierre plays a lot of prevent. However, neither Pierre nor I can handle agg rushes each turn, so Pierre is keen to let me oust Fred. In exchange, he has my votes on his Alastor. Tim who plays a lot of rush and combat cards and some intercept negotiates that Pierre doesn't use the Assault Rifle he's fetching against him, otherwise he would block (we'll know later that it was a bluff).
In the meantime, Arnaud gets Victor Pelletier out (Justicar) and steals 5 pool from me with a Parity Shift, then brings out more vampires.
I manage to survive with a few deflections while dealing damage to Fred, and in fact most of the table (Ancilla, Kine, but also a Political Stranglehold and an Ancient Influence)
I finally manage to oust Fred. Then, a turn later maybe, I launch a bleed for 6 on Pierre who deflects on Tim who deflects on Arnaud who deflects... back on Pierre. Basically, that bleed will kill Pierre. The fact that Pierre had helped me all game long with his votes kind of annoyed Arnaud who wasn't able to pass a single vote after his first Parity Shift. Pierre is ousted on a second bleed, but Arnaud won't have the time to benefit from his newfound vote lock since he's ousted on the next turn by Tim.
Trouble is that Tim is low on pool too, and he exhausted all his defensive resources on a vote I called on my turn (I think we went up to 5 stealth), then had to full-lock to oust Arnaud. He tries to make me believe he has some wakes left, but he doesn't so I oust him.

Tim 1VP
Vincent 4VP

NB: Pierre's seating was, according to his words, not optimal, but he had some grudge against Tim from an ancient tournament

Prince of Paris, France
